identity.title: Chain of Thought Monitorability: A New and Fragile Opportunity for AI Safety

title.before: What if automating AI R&D triggers an intelligence explosion?
title.after: Chain of Thought Monitorability: A New and Fragile Opportunity for AI Safety

abstract.before: In contrast to even a year ago, AI systems now write most of the code inside the companies that build them. As more of the AI research and development (R&D) pipeline is automated, could AI progress radically accelerate in an "intelligence explosion," where years of advances are compressed into months or less? Preliminary evidence suggests that it could. In this work, we assess this evidence, analyze an intelligence explosion's potential impacts, and propose policy responses. AI systems are on track to automate most AI R\&D work within a few years, and possibly all of it. If this triggers an intelligence explosion, it could dramatically bring forward AI's benefits, but also pose extreme risks: capabilities growth could accelerate far beyond what society can keep up with, humanity could lose control over superhuman AI systems, and checks on power within and between states, companies, and branches of government could be severely eroded. Although there remains much uncertainty about these possibilities, the high stakes warrant serious further attention. Policymakers should urgently obtain more visibility into the automation of AI R&D, develop ways to steer and constrain an intelligence explosion, and prepare society to adapt to an intelligence explosion's impacts.
abstract.after: AI systems that "think" in human language offer a unique opportunity for AI safety: we can monitor their chains of thought (CoT) for the intent to misbehave. Like all other known AI oversight methods, CoT monitoring is imperfect and allows some misbehavior to go unnoticed. Nevertheless, it shows promise and we recommend further research into CoT monitorability and investment in CoT monitoring alongside existing safety methods. Because CoT monitorability may be fragile, we recommend that frontier model developers consider the impact of development decisions on CoT monitorability.

scope_evidence_quotes.quote: We have in mind three settings where training for alignment seems especially prevalent and significant: socializing employees in a firm; socializing young people in families or communities; and training AI models.
The principal selects a set of states of the world in which to train the agent, subject to a maximum training budget
This paper has introduced and analyzed a simple model of training an agent to align their preferences.

independent_scope_evidence.quote: We propose a simple model of training an agent with an endogenous bias.
In response, the agent updates their bias and then acts optimally given their new bias in untrained states, while following their training in trained states.
Applications include socialization in organizations and families, and AI post-training and recursive self-improvement.
